title: Suitability and quality of the measures to maximise expected outcomes and impacts, as set out in the dissemination and exploitation plan, including communication activities
content:
## 2.2 Suitability and quality of the measures to maximise expected outcomes and impacts, as set out in the dissemination and exploitation plan, including communication activities

### Design logic: measures matched to a single-fellow action

FIELDWISE is a European Fellowship carried by one experienced researcher hosted at Eötvös Loránd University (ELTE), with three associated partners (MATE, MVCRI and AgroVIR) and a six-month non-academic placement at AgroVIR at the end of the 30-month action. The dissemination, exploitation and communication plan is therefore deliberately proportionate to what one fellow can deliver: every measure is anchored to a named project output or a named activity that already sits in the work plan, and none is promised beyond the resources of a single fellowship. Two design commitments run through the whole plan. First, project outputs are handled on the principle "as open as possible, as closed as necessary", so that openness is the default and closure is the justified exception rather than the reverse. Second, each impact route is carried by a tracked key performance indicator drawn from the confirmed set K1 to K11, so that the plan can be verified rather than merely asserted. This sub-section also discharges a specific commitment made in response to the previous evaluation of an earlier submission, which criticised that the economic and technological route to users and the IP strategy were insufficiently substantiated; the exploitation route and the IP treatment below are the direct answer to that criticism.

### Dissemination to scientific audiences

Scientific dissemination targets four principal scientific outputs: physiological and hyperspectral early-warning signatures of processing-tomato water stress; hyperspectral-to-Sentinel scaling for water-stress prediction; temporal and cross-country transferability of agricultural water-stress models; and research-to-commercial transfer and decision-oriented evaluation of agricultural AI. At least two high-quality peer-reviewed submissions are targeted during or shortly following the fellowship, with at least one open-access article per project year. The primary target group for these outputs is the agricultural remote-sensing and plant-physiology research community — Earth-observation-for-agriculture scientists and hyperspectral proximal-sensing researchers — for whom the physiology-to-satellite bridge is the novel contribution.

Beyond publications, dissemination is carried by the release of concrete, reusable research assets. The Hyperspectral-to-Sentinel transfer library (D2.2) is released with documented transferability verdicts — every candidate hyperspectral feature carrying an explicit transferable or hyperspectral-only verdict (KPI K2) — and the FIELDWISE predictive engine/model card (D3.2) is released with a published model card (KPI K4). These are aimed at European research organisations and precision-agriculture model developers seeking reusable transfer features and forecasting engines. The Hungary→Bulgaria transferability report (D4.2) and the Adaptation protocol (D4.3), which states the minimum local-calibration volume needed to move the model to a new agro-environment (KPI K6), are shared with the international partner MVCRI and the wider Bulgarian and Hungarian processing-tomato research and advisory community. The Harmonised historical database (D1.1), due in month 6, is curated to be FAIR with documented QC flags and metadata (KPI K1). Consistent with the Horizon Europe and MSCA open-science requirements the call sets out, the expected open outputs include harmonisation protocols, validation split manifests, the hyperspectral-to-Sentinel methodology, analysis and model code where IP permits, model cards, FAIR metadata, selected derived or anonymised datasets and open-access publications, with data management planned to Horizon Europe open-science standards. Together these measures advance the expected outcomes on enhanced networking and knowledge transfer (EO-07) and the corresponding impact on increased R&I capacity, output and knowledge transfer among European research organisations (EI-05).

### Communication and public engagement

Communication reaches beyond scientific peers to processing-tomato growers and farm advisors working with AgroVIR, and to the interested general agricultural public. Two concrete measures serve this group: one public field demonstration of the web MVP with AgroVIR farmers, and one public-facing article per project year. These measures were adopted specifically to address the expected impact on broadened public engagement with research and innovation (EI-03) and the expected outcome on enhanced networking and communication capacities with peers and with the general public (EO-03); the draft addresses neither of these on its own, so the measures are recorded honestly as operator-decided activities that carry no deliverable identifier rather than being attached to a fabricated deliverable. Science communication is one of the seven transferable-skill strands of the Career Development Plan set out in sub-section 2.1 and is not repeated here. Research results are also fed back into higher education through the co-design and delivery of a full module unit within an ELTE MSc course on Earth observation for agriculture, and the co-supervision of the field-experiment component of one PhD student's work — measures that serve the expected outcome on regular feedback of research results into teaching (EO-08) and the impact on enhanced integration of research results into teaching at host organisations (EI-06).

### Exploitation: from validated research to an operational route

Exploitation converts the science into a usable capability while remaining honest about how far a fellowship can carry it. The desktop research prototype is advanced to a scientifically validated DrR web MVP (D5.1), delivered by month 24 and serving stress probability, uncertainty, spatial risk, irrigation priority and temporal evolution (KPI K7). The MVP is then externally evaluated by AgroVIR through the AgroVIR functional/technical evaluation (D5.4), which covers all nine assessment dimensions (KPI K9) and, together with the Field Decision Value report (D5.3, KPI K8), supplies evidence about whether the technology meets actual agricultural software requirements and whether it delivers field-level decision value under commercial farming conditions. The transferable assets — the Hyperspectral-to-Sentinel transfer library (D2.2), the FIELDWISE predictive engine/model card (D3.2) and the Adaptation protocol (D4.3) — are packaged for reuse by other agro-environments beyond the Hungary and Bulgaria test cases. The exploitation chain terminates in the FMIS integration roadmap (D5.5), delivered in month 30, which names the required interfaces and the post-fellowship steps needed to embed FIELDWISE outputs into farm management information systems (KPI K10). This gives the project a research-to-operation delivery path with a named post-MSCA FMIS integration route (outcome OC5). The exploitation plan is deliberately bounded: the MVP is the research-to-operation demonstrator, not the primary scientific objective, and full commercial integration is not promised within the fellowship. The six-month AgroVIR placement is what makes this operational-transfer half structural rather than asserted, because the operational hardening, the nine-dimension assessment and the roadmap all depend on the company's own production environment and customer-facing requirements. These measures carry the scientific, technological and European impacts of the project (IMP-SCI, IMP-TECH, IMP-EU) and strengthen international, inter-sectoral and interdisciplinary collaboration (EI-02).

### Sustainability beyond the fellowship

The plan includes concrete actions that persist after the action ends. The released predictive engine with its model card (D3.2) and the Harmonised historical database (D1.1) remain maintained, FAIR research outputs held at ELTE; the Hyperspectral-to-Sentinel transfer library (D2.2) and the Adaptation protocol (D4.3) provide a documented, reusable method — with a stated minimum local-calibration cost — for transferring the approach to further crops and regions; the FMIS integration roadmap (D5.5), grounded in AgroVIR's external evaluation, defines the post-fellowship steps required to move the validated web MVP toward operational use; and the co-designed ELTE MSc module unit embeds the project's methods into ongoing higher-education teaching. Responsibility for sustaining these outputs is shared across ELTE, MATE, MVCRI and AgroVIR.

### Management of intellectual property and protection measures

As a single-beneficiary MSCA postdoctoral fellowship, FIELDWISE carries no bespoke consortium IP arithmetic, and the default position applies: results are owned by the host, ELTE, with the fellow as author-inventor, and open dissemination of scientific results — open-access publications, the released transfer library and the published model card — is the primary route to impact. Protection measures are proportionate and are invoked only where they are warranted. Where the web MVP or the predictive engine has commercialisation potential, protection would rely primarily on copyright in the software and on trade secrets around calibration data, with formal patenting considered only if the AgroVIR evaluation identifies protectable, novel technical subject matter. Access to and use of MVCRI and AgroVIR data are governed by the partners' agreed access conditions; commercially sensitive farmer data — yields, irrigation records and field geometries from AgroVIR farms — are handled under a data-sharing agreement and results are published only in aggregated or anonymised form. A specific background-IP boundary is managed explicitly: the DrR - Digital Agronomist components are the fellow's background IP, and the placement was structured as training-oriented work (operational hardening of the prediction pipeline, a structured operational assessment, authoring the FMIS integration roadmap from inside the implementing company, and requirements engineering and user testing with growers) rather than the development of the fellow's own prototype inside a commercial partner, precisely to keep the ownership boundary clean. The ownership of any results generated during the placement is to be settled by written agreement between the fellow, ELTE and AgroVIR; this arrangement is identified as a point to be formalised before the placement begins. This IP treatment, together with the AgroVIR-evaluated route to users, is the substantive answer to the previous evaluation's criticism that the economic and technological route to users and the IP strategy were insufficiently substantiated.

### Contribution to expected outcomes and impacts

Taken together, the measures form a coherent, verifiable and proportionate pathway to impact for a single fellowship: open, peer-reviewed dissemination and reusable released assets serve knowledge transfer among European research organisations (EO-07, EI-05); public demonstration and annual public-facing articles broaden engagement with research (EO-03, EI-03); teaching integration feeds results into higher education (EO-08, EI-06); the externally evaluated web MVP and the named FMIS integration route give the science an operational and inter-sectoral destination (EI-02, and the technological and European impacts of the project); and the IP treatment protects value without closing off the open-science route that is the fellowship's primary impact mechanism. Each route carries a tracked KPI and terminates in a named deliverable or a stated activity, so an evaluator can check that every claimed outcome has a concrete measure behind it, delivered during the action and sustained after it.
